column1: # POSIX external provider manifest.
# LICENSE POSTURE (this is why the file is shaped this way):
# MOST providers below are COPYLEFT — GPL-2.0, GPL-3.0, or the Vim license.
# Building those and hosting the BINARIES would make this project a distributor
# and trigger GPLv3 s6 / GPLv2 s3: convey corresponding source, build scripts
# and installation information, for every artifact, indefinitely.
# One row is permissive: lp (CUPS, Apache-2.0). Hosting that binary would
# trigger no source-conveyance duty. It is nevertheless fetched as source and
# built locally exactly like every other row. One policy for the whole table is
# auditable; two policies are a footgun that eventually mirrors the wrong row.
# So build and download are deliberately SEPARATED:
#   download -> UPSTREAM source only, pinned by sha256. Upstream is the
#               distributor; its obligations are already discharged.
#   build    -> LOCAL, from the recipe in build.sh. A binary you build for
#               yourself is not distribution, so no obligation is triggered.
#   we ship  -> this manifest and the recipe. Our own work, our own license.
# Never mirror or republish the built binaries. If an organisation chooses to
# host an internal prebuilt mirror, that is ITS distribution and it must ship
# the corresponding source alongside; this project does not.
# VERSIONS are pinned to exactly what the Profile A/B reference host runs, so a
# Profile C arm differs from A only in WHO supplies the command, never in which
# implementation. Re-pin only together with the reference image.
# sha256 is of the upstream artifact as downloaded, verified before extraction.
# An entry without a digest is REFUSED, never built.
# PLATFORMS is declared per provider and enforced. Cross-COMPILING is solved --
# one pinned Zig toolchain emits ELF, PE32+ and Mach-O from a single host, all
# verified. What varies per tool is CONFIGURING: autotools needs a POSIX shell,
# which Windows lacks natively. Three mechanisms exist, per tool:
#   - autotools cross-configure with --host=x86_64-w64-mingw32
#   - bashy itself as the POSIX shell, since it is a pure-Go bash 5.3 drop-in
#     with the Go coreutils supplying the unix tools (on-brand, unproven)
# A platform absent from a row is REFUSED, not attempted: better a clear refusal
# than an obscure configure failure. POSIX certification runs on Linux, so
# windows/darwin support is a product concern, never a certification blocker.
# command

# lp: CUPS 2.4.7 is exactly what Ubuntu 24.04 ships (cups-client 2.4.7-1.2ubuntu7.14),
# so the C arm and the GNU A arm run the same upstream release. Apache-2.0 read from
# cups-2.4.7/LICENSE in the pinned tarball (verbatim Apache License 2.0); cups-2.4.7/
# NOTICE adds CUPS-specific exceptions (Sections 4a/4b/4d waiver for embedded object
# code, and a GPLv2-combination waiver) which only widen the grant. Not windows: the
# client is POSIX-only (fork/exec, unix sockets) and upstream ships no Windows build.
# localedef: BUILDS, but it is the least ordinary row here and the reasons matter.
# Upstream has NO standalone build: localedef lives in glibc's locale/programs,
# and glibc/locale carries no configure of its own (verified against the
# glibc-2.39 tree) -- only a subdir Makefile the top-level build includes -- so
# upstream's only answer is "build all of glibc". The single-binary build used
# here is Yocto's cross-localedef-native path and needs THREE pinned inputs:
#   1. glibc 2.39 sources        the row above; ftp.gnu.org, digest verified by
#                                download-and-hash. GPL-2.0-or-later read from
#                                glibc-2.39/locale/programs/localedef.c, whose
#                                header says GPL version 2 or later -- note the
#                                locale PROGRAMS are GPL, not the library's LGPL.
#   2. github.com/kraj/localedef a ~14-file autotools harness compiling those
#                                sources against the host libc. No releases and
#                                no tags, so build.sh pins it by COMMIT.
#   3. four OpenEmbedded patches pinned by oe-core commit + per-file sha256.
# 0013 is load-bearing: it forward-ports eglibc's cross-locale support, and
# without it locale/localeinfo.h includes glibc-internal <tls.h> and the build
# stops dead. All four are Upstream-Status: Pending and have been carried out of
# tree since 2015 -- that staleness, not the build, is the standing risk.
# Re-pin the three together or not at all: the patches carry file-level context,
# so a glibc bump without a matching harness commit will fail to apply.
# WHY 2.39 EXACTLY, and why this is not pedantry: localedef writes binary locale
# data in a layout coupled to the libc that will read it, so a localedef from a
# different glibc can emit an archive the host mis-reads. 2.39 is what Ubuntu
# 24.04's libc-bin 2.39-0ubuntu8.8 is built from. Measured on ubuntu:24.04: the
# binary built by this recipe emits LC_CTYPE, LC_COLLATE, LC_TIME, LC_NUMERIC and
# LC_MONETARY BYTE-IDENTICAL to the host localedef's output for the same source,
# and the host libc loads them (locale charmap -> UTF-8, LC_TIME -> March).
# linux only: this compiles glibc's own sources against glibc. There is no
# darwin or windows build and there will not be one.
